from.place: Proof, first sentence: 'The cone C of alpha is zero if and only if alpha is an isomorphism'; also the final reduction for the pulled-back cone triangles.

title: Zero cone criterion for a distinguished triangle
statement: Let $\mathcal D$ be a pre-triangulated category [def-weil-triangulated-category], and let $X\xrightarrow{f}Y\xrightarrow{g}Z\xrightarrow{h}X[1]$ be a distinguished triangle in $\mathcal D$. Then $f$ is an isomorphism if and only if $Z$ is a zero object (equivalently, $Z$ is isomorphic to the zero object of $\mathcal D$).
